newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah up, swaps ease in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah up, swaps ease in late trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah recovered against the dollar while swap points declined in slow late trading on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the rupiah recovered from early weakness despite ample rupiah supply. Overnight rates fell to four percent from 12.5 percent in the morning.
One European bank dealer said trading was a bit slow in the afternoon, with the rupiah gaining back some ground after local operators countered offshore selling.
He said swap points also declined after rising earlier on worries of an attack on the Philippines peso.
"The attack on the peso seemed to have cooled down a bit. So did our swap points," the dealer said, adding that excess rupiah supply was also responsible for the easing.
Dealers said early spillover was not as strong as when offshore operators launched an attack on the Thai baht.
The European bank dealer said local operators were seen selling dollars on any offshore purchase, cooling brief early jitters after the peso was attacked.
Spot rupiah rose to 2,431.0/31.6 at 0915 GMT from a low of 2,433.25 after opening at 2,431.5/32.5. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,430.6/31.2 and 2,431.1/31.6, respectively.
Another dealer said there was still some speculation in the market of a widening of the central bank intervention band which sustained upward pressure on the rupiah.
Overnight swap was at 0.50/0.55 and tom/next at 0.30/0.35.
One-month swaps eased to 14.0/14.5 from 14.50/15.25, two to 27.5/29.0 from 28.75/29.50, three to 44.5/45.5 from 45.0/45.5.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,429/2,621 and the conversion band at 2,429/2,477 on Wednesday.
